key_insight: Intensity normalisation affects 3D knee MRI segmentation generalisability, but its benefit is modest compared with the larger impact of cross-dataset domain shift.
clinical_relevance: For deploying MRI segmentation models more reliably across scanners and protocols, normalisation can help, but it is not sufficient on its own to ensure robust external performance.
method: Compared seven intensity normalisation methods, including standard scaling, histogram-based techniques, and a GMM-based approach.
Trained a 3D U-Net for meniscus segmentation on the IWOAI 2019 dataset.
Evaluated performance on internal and external test sets (SKM-TEA) to assess generalisability.
evidence_signal: Internal performance was similar across methods, but external testing showed significant differences, with Z-score, Nyúl histogram matching, and CLAHE performing more robustly.
watch_item: Results suggest that choosing a normalisation method may help, but external-domain performance still drops substantially, so implementation should account for broader domain shift.
paper_title: A Systematic Benchmark of Intensity Normalisation Methods for 3D Knee MRI Segmentation and Cross-Domain Generalisability
